name: Audionaut
one_liner: A free, open-source multitrack audio editor that AI agents can drive over MCP, for music, podcasts and recording.

text.why: Cutting and arranging music or podcasts in a full DAW can be heavy and complex. Audionaut offers precise cutting, per-track playlists, multi-channel support and clean exports without that weight.
text.take: As in the README's demo, you can tell an agent 'cut clip every 16 bars'.
build: A desktop app built in C++ on JUCE that runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Connect an agent such as Claude over MCP and it edits the open project, with each edit as one undo step. It also analyses beats and segments.

who.role: People who edit podcasts, music or recordings and want something light.

start.text: Get the app from audionaut.app; for agents, use the README's claude mcp add command (Node.js 18+).

caveat: Dual-licensed under GPL-3.0 (or later) and a commercial licence, and contributions require a CLA. On macOS the README asks you to keep projects in your Music folder.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
